create_bar_chart.description: Draw a bar chart from labels and one or more series of numbers: vertical or horizontal, grouped or stacked, optionally with each bar's value on it and a prefix or suffix such as $ or % on the numbers. Returns a link to the picture that shows it in any email, chat message or document, an HTML image tag, and the picture as a file if asked.
create_bar_chart.name: create_bar_chart

parameters.description: The name of each bar, or group of bars, in order, separated by commas (or one per line), such as Q1, Q2, Q3. A list works too.
parameters.name: labels

parameters.description: One or more series, each with a name for the legend and its values, one for each label. Several series are drawn side by side, or stacked.
parameters.name: series

name.description: The series' name, shown in the legend.

values.description: The series' numbers, one for each label, separated by commas, such as 10, 20, 30. Leave one empty for a gap.

parameters.description: Text above the chart. A line break in it starts a second line. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Draw the bars across instead of up, the first at the top. Off by default.
parameters.name: horizontal

parameters.description: Stack several series' bars on top of each other instead of side by side. Off by default.
parameters.name: stacked

parameters.description: Write each bar's value on it. Off by default.
parameters.name: show_values

parameters.description: Text before each number on the value axis, and on the bars' values, such as $ or EUR. Up to 10 characters, without *, commas or |.
parameters.name: value_prefix

parameters.description: Text after each number on the value axis, and on the bars' values, such as % or k. Up to 10 characters, without *, commas or |.
parameters.name: value_suffix

parameters.description: One colour for each series, as hex codes such as #4E79A7 or names such as navy, separated by commas; with a single series, several colours colour its bars one by one. Anything left over takes a ten-colour palette.
parameters.name: colors

parameters.description: Where the legend of series names goes: bottom (the default), right, top or left, or no legend. There is only a legend when a series has a name.
parameters.name: legend_position

parameters.description: The chart's width in pixels, from 1 to 999. Defaults to 600.
parameters.name: width

parameters.description: The chart's height in pixels, from 1 to 999. Defaults to 400.
parameters.name: height

parameters.description: The colour behind the chart, as a hex code such as #FFFFFF, a name such as white, or transparent. White if left empty.
parameters.name: background_color

parameters.description: Draw the chart growing into place as an animated GIF, for an email or a chat message. Off by default. A GIF is several times the size of the still picture.

parameters.description: Off by default, because the link is all an email, a chat message or a document needs. Turn it on when a later step needs the file itself: attaching it to an email, uploading it to storage, or posting it as a file.

image_tag.description: The same link as an HTML tag, with alt text and the chart's width and height, for a step that writes an email or a page.

saved_as_file.description: True when the chart was also saved as a file (Also save the chart as a file). The file fields below are empty otherwise.

watermarked.description: True when Image-Charts drew its small watermark in the top right corner: every chart but a QR code, unless the connection has an Image-Charts account.

width.description: The width in pixels the chart is shown at, as asked for. A diagram is shown at its own size. Chart.js charts and QR codes are drawn with more pixels than this, so they stay sharp.

create_radar_chart.description: Draw a radar (spider) chart comparing one or more series across three or more labels, one spoke each, such as skills or product scores, optionally shading inside each series. Returns a link to the picture, an HTML image tag, and the picture as a file if asked.
create_radar_chart.name: create_radar_chart

parameters.description: The name of each spoke, in order round the chart from the top, separated by commas (or one per line). At least 3.
parameters.name: labels

parameters.description: One or more series, each with a name for the legend and its values, one for each spoke.
parameters.name: series

name.description: The series' name, shown in the legend.

values.description: The series' numbers, one for each label, separated by commas, such as 10, 20, 30. Leave one empty for a gap.

parameters.description: Text above the chart. A line break in it starts a second line. Leave empty for none.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Shade the area inside each series. Off by default.
parameters.name: fill

parameters.description: One colour for each series, in order, as hex codes such as #4E79A7 or names such as navy, separated by commas. Series without one take the next colour of a ten-colour palette.
parameters.name: colors

parameters.description: Where the legend of series names goes: bottom (the default), right, top or left, or no legend. There is only a legend when a series has a name.
parameters.name: legend_position

parameters.description: The chart's width in pixels, from 1 to 999. Defaults to 400.
parameters.name: width

parameters.description: The chart's height in pixels, from 1 to 999. Defaults to 400.
parameters.name: height

parameters.description: The colour behind the chart, as a hex code such as #FFFFFF, a name such as white, or transparent. White if left empty.
parameters.name: background_color

parameters.description: Draw the chart growing into place as an animated GIF, for an email or a chat message. Off by default. A GIF is several times the size of the still picture.
parameters.name: animated

parameters.description: Off by default, because the link is all an email, a chat message or a document needs. Turn it on when a later step needs the file itself: attaching it to an email, uploading it to storage, or posting it as a file.

description: Turn data into chart pictures for emails, chat messages and documents with Image-Charts: bar, line, pie, doughnut, radar and scatter charts, sparklines, progress bars, QR codes, GraphViz diagrams and Chart.js charts. Each comes back as a permanent link that shows the picture anywhere an image can go, with an HTML image tag, and can be saved as a file. Works without an account, with a small watermark and up to 10 charts a minute; an Image-Charts subscription's account ID and secret key remove the watermark and raise the limit.
